sections.body: Discovery AI is now judged by clinical results, not demos. The candidates reaching patients came from teams that paired models with their own experimental data and wet lab loops, so data quality and lab integration decide more than the choice of model.
sections.heading: What it means for a life sciences team

siblings.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

explainer:
Drug discovery is the slow, expensive search for a molecule that hits the right biological target without causing harm. Traditionally it meant screening huge chemical libraries and testing thousands of compounds in the lab, with most failing. AI changes the search in three ways.

First, prediction. Models such as AlphaFold predict the three dimensional shape of proteins and how molecules bind to them, work that once took months of laboratory effort per structure. Second, generation. Generative models propose new molecules and antibodies designed for a target, rather than finding them in an existing library. Third, prioritisation. Models rank which candidates are worth making and testing, so scarce laboratory time goes to the most promising ones.

None of this removes the laboratory. Every AI prediction still has to be confirmed by experiment, and the strongest programmes run a loop in which models propose, robots test, and the results train better models. That is why large drugmakers are investing in their own compute, lab automation and data, and why partnerships between pharma companies and AI biotechs have become the main way the industry buys this capability.

The evidence so far is encouraging on speed, AI derived candidates have reached the clinic faster than usual, but whether AI improves the chance that a drug ultimately works in patients is still being tested in later stage trials.
key_points: Structure prediction, molecule generation and candidate ranking are the three main uses.
Every prediction still needs experimental confirmation; closed lab loops are the leading model.
Drugmakers are building compute and lab automation and partnering with AI biotechs.
AI has shortened time to the clinic; its effect on success rates is not yet proven.

developments.text: Lilly and NVIDIA announced a co-innovation lab to apply AI and large scale compute across drug discovery, using NVIDIA BioNeMo and Vera Rubin systems.

Rentosertib, Insilico Medicine's AI discovered TNIK inhibitor, raised mean forced vital capacity by 98.4 mL over 12 weeks against a 20.3 mL decline on placebo in a phase 2a trial in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Isomorphic Labs, the Alphabet drug design company spun out of DeepMind, raised $600 million in its first outside funding to advance its AI design engine and take programmes into the clinic.
Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs released AlphaFold 3, which predicts the structure and interactions of proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules.
